    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a notably hawkish speech at Jackson Hole, signalling further rate hikes may be needed due to inflation remaining too high, non-restrictive financial conditions, and a full-employment labour market. Barclays revised its outlook, now expecting two 25bps hikes in September and December, reversing its prior hold forecast. Markets are pricing a 60.4% probability of a September hike, with the next key decision date set for September 16.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES (YES — directly covers Fed rate policy, Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, Barclays' revised rate outlook, and live market pricing via CME FedWatch)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 95 (95 — the entire article centers on Barclays' expectation of two additional hikes and Warsh's hawkish tightening signals)
Probability of increase: 60.4% (market-implied per CME FedWatch for September; Barclays baseline now calls for hikes in both September and December)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (10 — holding is only referenced as Barclays' prior, now-abandoned baseline)
Probability of holding: 39.6% (residual implied probability from CME FedWatch, i.e. 100% minus 60.4%)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (0 — cuts are not mentioned or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (80 — Warsh's speech is characterized as "notably hawkish," Barclays flipped from hold to two hikes, market pricing shifted upward post-speech, and base effects are flagged as a headwind to disinflation through year-end; all signals point firmly in a tightening direction with no dovish offset present)
